analysis.title: The Weekly Brief (Market Insights, 2 November 2026)
key_insights: Global 2027 EPS growth expectations have risen by a few percentage points this year. The latest estimate is tracking at 17% y/y, well above trend growth.
Technology accounts for most of the 2027 global EPS growth upgrade. It offsets large growth downgrades in energy, communication services and consumer discretionary.
The communication services and consumer discretionary downgrades appear to reflect adverse base effects after blockbuster Q2 earnings from some mega-cap AI-related names, not weaker outlooks.

Most other sectors' 2027 EPS growth estimates have been relatively stable this year. If economic growth picks up and energy prices fall, those sectors and the headline EPS figure could see further upgrades.
Last week, communication services fell 6.7% and technology fell 1.3%, while healthcare rose 3.1%. Growth lagged value by 1.8 percentage points (-1.1% vs +0.7%).
Brent is at $115/bbl, up 89.0% YTD. The US 10-year yield is 4.91%, down 9bps on the week. Gold is at $3,896/oz, down 2.5% on the week.
Week ahead: US midterm elections on Tuesday, a Bank of England decision on Thursday (prior 3.75%), and US October non-farm payrolls on Friday (prior 29k).

earnings_insights: MSCI All Country World 2027 EPS growth estimate is tracking at 17% y/y (IBES consensus data as of 28 October 2026), up a few percentage points over the year.
